reason: Returning a phone number from customers.lookup@1 would require a contract change. The contract declares exactly five outputs: /customerId, /name, /email, /tier and /since. There is no phone field. The rule output.return-no-more says the capability may 'return only what the current output schema allows', so adding a /phone output to the handler (src/handlers/customers.lookup.mjs) would break the contract. That makes this a contract change, not an implementation change. It would need a new output field with its type, whether it is required, its format and its concept, which probably means a new version (customers.lookup@2) so the dependents billing.contact@1 and customers.register@1 are not affected. A separate problem is that the contract declares no verification methods (evidence.establishable is false), so even an allowed implementation change here could not be verified. Suggested next step: whoever owns the contract defines the phone output, likely in a new capability version, and then the handler can be updated against that contract.
